subject: math.CO
name: Hadwiger conjecture
statement: For every integer k≥1, every finite simple graph with chromatic number at least k contains the complete graph K_k as a minor. A minor is obtained by deleting vertices or edges and contracting edges.
importance: A central proposed link between graph coloring and graph minors.
status_note: The general conjecture remains open; the cases k≤6 are proved.

subject: math.CO
name: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
statement: For every fixed finite graph H, there is ε(H)>0 such that every n-vertex graph with no induced copy of H has either a clique or an independent set of size at least n^ε(H).
importance: Predicts unexpectedly strong structure in graphs excluding an induced subgraph.
status_note: Many forbidden graphs are understood, but the assertion for arbitrary H remains open.

subject: math.CO
name: Graceful tree conjecture
statement: Every finite tree with m edges admits a bijective labeling of its vertices by 0,…,m such that the absolute differences of labels across its edges are exactly 1,…,m.
importance: A foundational graph-labeling conjecture with links to graph decompositions.
status_note: Many families of trees and large finite ranges have been verified; arbitrary trees remain unresolved.

subject: math.CO
name: Lovász Hamiltonian-path conjecture
statement: Every finite connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path, a path visiting every vertex exactly once. Vertex-transitive means that graph automorphisms can send any vertex to any other.
importance: A central question about whether symmetry forces spanning paths in graphs.
status_note: Many Cayley-graph and other symmetric families are understood; the general Hamiltonian-path assertion remains open.

subject: math.CO
name: Tutte five-flow conjecture
statement: Every finite bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow: orient its edges and assign each a nonzero integer of absolute value less than 5 so that total incoming and outgoing values agree at each vertex.
importance: One of the central unsolved flow problems in graph theory.
status_note: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow; replacing 6 by 5 remains open in general.

subject: math.CO
name: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
statement: Every finite bridgeless cubic graph has six perfect matchings, allowing repetition, such that each edge belongs to exactly two of the matchings.
importance: A sharp structural conjecture linking perfect matchings, edge coloring, and cycle covers.
status_note: Cubic means every vertex has degree three; the bridgeless hypothesis is essential.

subject: math.CO
name: Ryser conjecture on Latin transversals
statement: Every Latin square of odd order n has a transversal: n cells with one in each row and column, containing each symbol exactly once.
importance: A major matching problem underlying Latin squares and combinatorial designs.
status_note: Results on near-transversals and special classes do not resolve the full odd-order assertion.

subject: math.CO
name: Union-closed sets conjecture
statement: For every finite family of finite sets that is closed under unions and contains a nonempty set, some element occurs in at least half the sets in the family.
importance: A deceptively elementary extremal-set problem with broad influence.
status_note: Recent constant-fraction lower bounds do not reach the required one-half bound in general.

subject: math.CO
name: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
statement: Every finite simple directed graph on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least r≥1 contains a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/r).
importance: A basic proposed relationship between local directed degree and short cycles.
status_note: The general conjecture is open, including important cases demanding a directed triangle.

references.title: A Summary of Problems and Results related to the Caccetta–Häggkvist Conjecture

subject: math.CO
name: Graph reconstruction conjecture
statement: Every finite simple graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of unlabeled graphs obtained by deleting one vertex at a time.
importance: Asks whether all local vertex-deletion views determine a graph globally.
status_note: The restriction to at least three vertices is necessary; numerous graph classes are reconstructible.
